#3744. The Borderlands series has sold over 100 million copies, and Gearbox is "cooking hard on more Borderlands 4 content for next year"

The Borderlands series has sold more than 100m copies across all games, developer Gearbox Software has announced. No surprise, then - the studio also said it's cooking up "big plans" for the evergreen looter shooter's future.

"The Borderlands franchise has officially crossed 100 million units sold," Gearbox boasted in a blog post published today. "There aren't many franchises that have ever hit that milestone, and we certainly didn't get here on our own. For us, it started with that first Borderlands in 2009, and we've been excited about everyone who has joined us in the Borderlands along the way. Borderlands has always had an incredibly passionate community. We've been through a lot together, and your feedback pushes us to make even greater games."

So, where can Vault Hunters expect to go next? Gearbox just finished up on Borderlands 4's Year One roadmap - which included two new playable characters, two Story Packs and more - and it's now "cooking hard on more Borderlands 4 content for next year." There's no concrete information about what that looks like for now, but the studio promised Weekly Activity refreshes and Community Challenges will chug on in the meantime.

"We're also taking a bigger look at the franchise as a whole. Where can we take it next? What characters do you want to spend more time with? What stories deserve a payoff? A huge part of that is listening to you," the studio wrote. "All that said, big plans take time, and we need some room to work. You can trust that we'll talk more when the time is right. Now is your chance to influence what we'll say."

Borderlands 4 itself experienced a "softer" than expected launch, thanks partly to the game's wonky PC performance, though it seems to have been a success in the long run. A promised Switch 2 port was also indefinitely delayed earlier in the year. We haven't heard much about that handheld version since, but Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick did say the team were focusing on getting Borderlands 4 into tip-top shape before trying to bring it elsewhere.

In Eurogamer's Borderlands 4 review, Rick Lane said the shooter bought a "more sensible script and a true open world to its pseudo-cel-shaded gun-show, but these moderate improvements are undermined by frustrating exploration and combat that takes too long to properly shine."

#3743. Elder Scrolls 6 Gets Its First New Teaser Trailer In Over 8 Years, But Still No Release Date

To celebrate 40 years of Bethesda Game Studios, the company released a short video looking back on its history while also teasing the future. At the end of that video, Bethesda confirmed the previously reported claim that Elder Scrolls 6 is titled Sentinel. But if you were expecting a release date, well…bad news.

On Tuesday, Bethesda creative director Todd Howard presented a small look back at 40 years of Bethesda history. Then, at the end of the video, Howard mentioned that it was a “perfect time” to look forward.

“You know, everybody’s always asking about Elder Scrolls 6,” said Howard. “And we thought, hey, given the moment, what a perfect time to tell you what The Elder Scrolls 6 is actually called.”

After that, a brief teaser plays, revealing a scroll buried in sand, before finally confirming that the title of Bethesda’s next big RPG is indeed Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, as many fans expected.

In Elder Scrolls lore, Sentinel is the name of a major city located in Hammerfell, which is believed to be the main setting of this upcoming entry in the long-running RPG series. A previous report claimed the game would reveal more about the ancient origins of the titular Elder Scrolls, and the teaser above, featuring a scroll being pulled from the sand, seems to suggest that report was accurate.

In June 2026, Howard seemed to indicate the RPG was possibly still years away from release and that it was too early for a “re-reveal.” I guess a name reveal is different.

This is the first new teaser for Elder Scrolls 6 since Bethesda first announced the RPG about eight years ago at E3 2018. At the time, Bethesda didn’t provide a release date or even a rough window. In the many years since, Howard has claimed that he regrets that the studio announced it so early. Considering the fact that nearly a decade has passed since that first teaser and The Elder Scrolls 6 still doesn’t have a release date, yeah, it does seem like Bethesda revealed the RPG far too soon.

Since 2018, a lot has happened in the game industry, including the slow death of E3 itself. And just two years after announcing TES6, Bethesda was bought by Xbox for $7.5 billion. Meanwhile, Bethesda launched Starfield in 2023 to mixed reviews from both fans and critics. Earlier this year, Xbox made big cuts to Bethesda while also announcing big plans for Fallout, including a New Vegas remaster and a new Obsidian Entertainment-developed entry in the RPG series.Â

Spoilers ahead for the Season 4 premiere of The Gilded Age.

Shortly after its premiere, The Gilded Age joined the ranks of HBO shows that got the world talking. Luckily for fans of the period piece, Season 4 has finally arrived on the network (and streaming with a HBO Max subscription). While the show sometimes gets flak online for not having enough drama, I'll admit the premiere episode had me biting my nails for two different reasons. Let's break it all down.

It remains to be seen if The Gilded Age finally gets a Downton Abbey crossover, but Season 4 started off with a bang. The premiere was titled "Ring the Bells" and put two major characters in peril.

The first of which was Louisa Jacobson's Marian Brook. After attending the after party of Oscar van Rhijn and Enid Winterton's wedding, Marian gets into a carriage with Larry Russell. The horse gets spooked by the storm, starts running out of control. I really thought they were going to get into an accident, but it turns out that the real "danger" was Marian losing her inhibitions and the pair sleeping together at a hotel. She's now worried about the news getting out, and her reputation (and chances at marriage) being ruined forever. Different set of stakes, but I'll take it.

Then there was the drama with Taissa Farmiga's Gladys. She was shown struggling to give birth in the Season 4 premiere, and I thought for a minute that the character might end up being killed off. The stakes got even higher when she started hemorrhaging from the breech birth, and let's just say that I didn't have faith in the medicine of 1880s enough to save her life.

Luckily both she and her young son survived the birth, but not without sacrifice. The doctor ended up performing a hysterectomy to save her life, meaning that she (obviously) can no longer get pregnant. While not life-threatening, but potentially puts her marriage to The Duke in jeopardy. If something happens to their child he might be inspired to find another wife who can help produce an heir.

Fans want a number of Gilded Age characters to make a splash in Season 4, and it should be interesting to see how things play out. The Gilded Age Season 4 already seems like its making some big changes to the beloved series, and I'm eager to see how things shake out over the next few months.

The Gilded Age airs new episodes Sundays on HBO as part of the 2026 TV schedule. Folks who thought the show doesn't have enough drama might want to tune back in and see if they change their mind.

#3741. Yakuza creator's new studio and its debut game Gang of Dragon are no more after losing funding from NetEase

Nagoshi Studio has officially shut down and its first game called Gang of Dragon is seemingly no more, months after publisher NetEase pulled funding from the Yakuza-like project.

Toshihiro Nagoshi (often cited as the creator of the brilliant Yakuza and Like A Dragon game series) opened his new studio in 2021 and announced his next game with a very familiar title almost one year ago. Now, the Tokyo-based developer has closed its doors, as confirmed in the Japanese government gazette Kanpo.

The news comes months after employees were told that the studio's future was at risk due to NetEase's funding cuts. Nagoshi Studio reportedly needed another £33.1 million (about $44.4m at the time) to get Gang of Dragon past the finish line - a paycheck NetEase purportedly didn't want to cough up.

The China-based Marvel Rivals and Where Winds Meet publisher has been significantly scaling back on international investments these past few years. Visions of Mana developer Ouka Studios was shut down just after launching its gorgeous action game, Worlds Untold (a studio formed by Mass Effect veteran Mac Walters) had to pause operations to find a new partner, and Halo Infinite lead Jerry Hook's studio also ran into very similar issues last year.

Some developers have been a little luckier. Suda51's Grasshopper Manufacture saved itself with a management buyout and now operates as an independent developer, for one.

Not much is known about Gang of Dragon, but its debut trailer featured the violent crime and high drama you'd expect from Nagoshi's previous work. The game also starred Ma Dong-seok, the acclaimed actor you might recognise from films such as Train to Busan and Marvel's Eternals.

This week, Bethesda Game Studios is celebrating its 40th birthday—a celebration that included the full name reveal of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, successfully completing the eight-year task of adding a word to a thing.

In addition, Bethesda is commemorating the occasion with the launch of a 40th anniversary site collecting the anecdotes and favorite memories of studio staff, including one Alan Nanes. Now a design director, Nanes was originally hired at Bethesda as one of its first full-time QA testers—and by his own description, he got the job by being a pleasant fellow to spend time with.

According to Nanes, his history with Bethesda started during Morrowind's development. He was close friends with Bethesda devs in multiple departments, and it was an era where that was enough to get you in the building.

"Things were a bit 'Wild West' back then, and my friends allowed me to hang out (yes, before I was an employee) there, playing multiplayer games with them and just getting to know everyone," Nanes wrote. "Eventually, Todd Howard noticed my presence in the studio and asked if I wanted to test out their new game."

In time, his impromptu testing sessions started attracting an audience of Bethesda developers who would pick his brain about their design choices, scribble notes, and debate with each other about potential tweaks to the game while watching over his shoulder.

"It was an extraordinary feeling, the first time I felt like I was contributing to the creation of an actual videogame (I believe you can find my name in the Morrowind manual's credits under 'Special Thanks')," Nanes said. "After this became a regular occurrence, Todd Howard and Ashley Cheng seemed to decide having full-time, in-studio QA would be a valuable addition to the team, and I took on that mantle."

Nanes later graduated to a quest designer position for Oblivion, and was more recently credited as lead companions designer on Starfield. But while his tenure at Bethesda might've had a storybook trajectory, the history of QA workers at the studio has been a contentious one in the years since Nanes was hired.

From the creators of Edge: A free weekly videogame industry newsletter, featuring in-depth news, expert analysis and exclusive interviews

Driven by frustrations surrounding compensation, advancement opportunities, workload, and more, QA workers at Bethesda's parent company ZeniMax initiated a unionization vote in 2022, officially forming ZeniMax Workers United - CWA—then the largest videogame union in the US—when the vote succeeded in January 2023.

Those frustrations remained unaddressed as contract negotiations with Microsoft stalled for over two years, driving the QA union to vote overwhelmingly in favor of authorizing a strike in April 2025. Its contract was ultimately ratified in June 2025. When a number of those QA workers were affected by Xbox's July 2026 layoffs, that contract allowed the union to enter into an "effects bargaining" process to negotiate severance terms for its impacted members, culminating in "a significant agreement" in September 2026.

#3739. Man Arrested in Girlfriend's Death Years After Body Found Burned in Field

A man has been arrested in connection to the cold case murder of his 20-year-old girlfriend, whose body was found burned and “extremely decomposed” in a Texas field nearly seven years ago.

Joey Emiliano Tovar-Vargas has been charged with tampering with evidence in the death of Meagan Gonzales, according to authorities.

“What we can prove at this point is that he disposed of her body,” Bexar County Sheriff Javier Salazar said during a Saturday, October 31, news conference.

Tovar-Vargas, 24, was arrested at his San Antonio home Saturday evening, according to Salazar.

Gonzales was last seen alive on November 11, 2019, when she was with Tovar-Vargas inside her truck on November 11, 2019.

Gonzales’ family members reported her missing four days later, after they couldn’t reach her, per the San Antonio Express-News. Her relatives told investigators Tovar-Vargas was her boyfriend.

Within a few weeks, Gonzales’ pickup truck was discovered December 2, 2019, with traces of blood in the truck bed, according to authorities. The blood was ultimately linked to Gonzales’ DNA.

The next day, Gonzales’ burned body was discovered in a field, wrapped in a blanket, in southwest Bexar County, Salazar said.

The blanket had a “distinctive pattern that factors into the case,” Salazar noted.

Tovar-Vargas had been considered a suspect during the early investigation into Gonzales’ death, but the case went cold after Salazar said investigators exhausted initial investigative leads.

In 2025, cold case investigators revisited the case using new technology and uncovered evidence linking Tovar-Vargas to Gonzales’ murder, Salazar said.

Phone records placed Tovar-Vargas near where Gonzales’ personal items were found discarded, as well as where her truck was abandoned, according to authorities.

Investigators also found searches in his cellphone, such as “how long do fingerprints last” and searches on “how to delete social media,” Salazar said.

Photos on Tovar-Vargas’ phone the blanket that had been wrapped around Gonzales’ body, according to Salazar. The images uncovered by investigators showed the blanket inside Tovar-Vargas’ home.

“Although we’re not yet there to the point where we’re able to charge him with murder, we would ask anybody with information to give us a call,” Salazar said of Tovar-Vargas during the news conference.

Tovar-Vargas is accused of asking a witness in the case to help move a body.

Information on whether he had retained legal counsel wasn’t immediately available.

Following Tovar-Vargas’ arrest, Gonzales’ father, Eddie Gonzales, told CBS affiliate KENS-TV that he visited an altar for his daughter.

“I told her, ‘Meagan, it looks like you’re getting your justice that I promised you,'” Eddie said. “Meagan, I hope you get some rest now, as I’m getting it.”

Sony's Bend Studio, perhaps one of its lesser discussed development houses, has apparently been deep in development on its next title. The game is reportedly set to be announced in 2027, and released in the same year.

That's according to MP1st, citing "people aware of what's happening at Bend". Like Days Gone, Bend's next game is in third-person. The title is said to include co-op support, but no live service elements.

The report doesn't say whether the game is based on a new IP or an existing one, but it does state that it's not a sequel to Days Gone. The game is apparently "much further along in development" than we realise, which isn't entirely surprising considering Bend has been quiet for years.

Two years later, a job post described a game in development at Bend as a triple-A live service project. That unannounced game was then cancelled in 2025, triggering a wave of layoffs at the studio that took place a few months later. Bend hasn't said a word since then.

It's now clear the studio hopped on its next project following the cancellation of that live service game. Seeing as 2026 is nearly over, we're not likely to be waiting much longer to see that mysterious game unveiled.

#3737. Arc Raiders Developers Try To Rationalize Using AI Voice Actors In Peculiar New Video

I’ve just finished point-and-click adventure Heir of the Dog. It’s really good! The main character, voiced by Tom Hardwidge, has perhaps 76 billion lines of dialog, and nails every single one. Meanwhile,Â Arc Raiders developer Embark says it absolutely had to use AI to voice characters in its relatively taciturn extraction shooter because “the actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that!”

As noticed byÂ RPS, a new video uploaded by developer Embark features CCO Stefan Strandberg and others at the studio explaining why Arc Raiders controversially included AI voice acting, and the reasons are…odd.

When the game launched in October of 2025, it had a bizarre mishmash of voice acting and genAI voices, which caused a fair amount of fuss. By March 2026, Embark announced it was beginning the process of replacing the AI voices with human ones, and now, another eight months later, it’s approaching the subject head-on in a video hosted by Danny O’Dwyer.

The core issue here is the repeated declaration that aspects that can make voice acting and recording arduous workâlike the many variants that are needed for delivering the public “pings” when you want to communicate in-context information in the fieldâare somehow now “too impractical to record every version of something.” Audio director Bence Pajor says, “The actors would go crazy if they had to read all of that.” This follows the last 30 years of voice actors recording astonishing numbers of lines for video games.

Midway through the video comes an awkward moment in which two of the game’s voice actors themselves appear to justify the use of AI, although it does seem like the words might not be entirely in context. Later the pair adds that on reflection, they wondered if they could “truly own” their performances when so much wasn’t actually them, and concluded no.

There are also some very weaselly explanations like, “After release there was an outcry from a number of players and games journalists about the use of AI to record these voices. At the time the studio kept silent about it, opting instead to put in the work to re-record lines with the voice actors as quickly as they could.”

Re-recording dialog is not something that’s only done when responding to a controversy, and the idea that staying silent allowed Embark to put in more work or do things more quickly is just silly.

Then comes another of the ol’ tricks, in which Pajor, laughing, points out people still complained about AI even when the lines were recorded by humans, which he says suggests, “Hey, you can’t even tell, so why does it matter?!” The reason it matters is that this is an industry move that will evaporate voice actors’ work and income at a net loss for quality and performance.

“We are not in the industry of replacing actors,” adds Strandberg. “Actually, I think it’s quite the opposite. We should celebrate the performance and we should give them more space.” Which is hard to take entirely to heart given the same video states that the removal of AI lines happened in response to the backlash.

Either way, it’s great that Embark is now taking the role of voice actors more seriously. Humans deserve better treatment than machines.

It's clear Julia Stiles is on the elimination bubble of Dancing With The Stars, after guest judge Shirley Ballas gave her a 4 on Halloween Night. While there's always a chance for competitors to bounce back after an off week, I think her song choice for Disney Night is only going to help her get sent home this week.

The song list for Disney Night dropped ahead of the annual episode on the 2026 TV schedule, and there are some questionable picks. Julia and Ezra Sosa's choice might be the strangest of them all, because I think plenty of fans will have something to say about a Hamilton song slipping through.

I know that Disney loves to remind us that Hamilton is available to stream with a Disney+ subscription, but it is not a stage production that originated from the House of Mouse. I'm sure that's why Julia and Ezra were allowed to pick "Satisfied" for their upcoming performance, but that doesn't make it any less aggravating.

There are too many good Disney movies to include a song from a project that doesn't originate from the studio. While it's true that contestants and pros have limited control over the songs they get during a season via a questionnaire, clearly that had to fill out something that ranked it high on the list to get it. Is Dancing With The Stars' Disney night just another vehicle for the company to cross-promote its other brands? Absolutely, but including a dance number for something that isn't inherently from it really kills the vibe.

It feels like the writing is on the wall for Julia Stiles on Dancing With The Stars. Now that viewers have seen her pay homage to Save The Last Dance as well as her tribute to Heath Ledger, they're now more concerned about her actual dancing.

I'm Watching Dancing With The Stars For The First Time, And Now I Am All In

Stiles had a standout performance with her contemporary dance and scored all nines. That said, when it comes to more traditional dances, she's struggled tremendously and hovered toward the bottom of the leaderboard most of the competition.

With the exception of Tatyana Ali, the rest of the Dancing With The Stars contestants are leaps and bounds ahead of her. Just from talking to various people who are watching this season, there seems to be a growing desire to keep Tatyana in the competition and let Julia's run come to an end.

We're deep into DWTS Season 35, so it's inevitable that favorites are going to go home. Only the best of the best should be in the finale, and if they aren't, the audience and judges have failed. As such, I think it's curtains for Julia this week, unless she puts on a truly stellar performance.

Disney Night is on ABC and Disney+ on November 2nd. Make note of the fact that it's a Monday night, as network television will be taken over by the midterm election results.

#3735. Remedy revenue soars by 226% following release of Control Resonant, the developer's fastest-selling game ever

Remedy - the developer behind the recently released Control Resonant - has released a scorcher of a quarterly financial report. It shows that following Resonant's release in September, the company's revenue surged by 226 percent, bringing in €39.6m in Q3.

This performance was described as "a defining milestone for the company" by CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon. The company reported a €0.6m operating profit this quarter, a fair leap upwards from the €16.4m loss from this time last year.

There are some interesting highlights to this sudden surging performance. For one, the US made up nearly half of Control Resonant's players across PC and console, followed by Chinese-speaking regions and then the UK.

Perhaps most crucially is that nearly half of Control Resonant's players were entirely new to the franchise, with the company stating: "Reaching new players was a key goal for this game, and these early results indicate a growing audience for the franchise and for Remedy."

Control (2019) also saw a bump up in sales thanks to the release of Control Resonant, showing a stronger performance this quarter than the past two quarters this year as well as its comparison period (this quarter last year).

Remedy's CEO now believes the focus for the studio is to "get Resonant into the hands of more players." He continues to say the game has provided a solid foundation for growth as other projects (including the Max Payne 1 & 2 remake) are in the works. In short, things appear to be looking rather good for Remedy.

Control Resonant was an artistically impressive but critically divisive game. While many praised the series' adventure into third person action, some felt it had less of a narrative bite than its predecessor. Nonetheless the game quickly blasted past one million sales after launch.

You might be thinking, if you're the optimistic sort, that today's official unveiling of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel means that wheels are turning and things are happening and you're going to be off to Hammerfell soon—or at the very least, learning more about what's coming in Bethesda's next big RPG. Alas, in a follow-up post on social media, the studio made it clear that you shouldn't start holding your breath just yet.

"Thank you for 40 years of shared memories," Bethesda wrote. "We can't wait to make even more together with The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Development continues, and while it'll be some time before we're ready to share more, it feels great to finally reveal the name and location with you."

Thank you for 40 years of shared memories. We can’t wait to make even more together with The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. Development continues, and while it’ll be some time before we’re ready to share more, it feels great to finally reveal the name and location with you.

"Some time" is obviously not a defined span, but I find that generally speaking it's a nicer, more politic way of saying "long time"—for instance, you could say it's been "some time" since Bethesda first announced the Elder Scrolls 6, and yeah, that's true. It was also eight freakin' years ago, and we've heard basically nothing since.

That is, very roughly, the same amount of time Bethesda needed to make the first Elder Scrolls game, Arena, as well as Daggerfall, Morrowind, the Morrowind expansions Tribunal and Bloodmoon, and the spinoff games Battlespire and Redguard. If you're (relatively) new to the series, eight years represents the span between Oblivion and The Elder Scrolls Online, a stretch interspersed by Skyrim and five major expansions: Knights of the Nine and Shivering Isles for Oblivion, and Dawnguard, Hearthfire, and Dragonborn for Skyrim.

Of course, Bethesda's had other things on the go over the past eight years too. Todd Howard said shortly after The Elder Scrolls 6 reveal that it was in pre-production, while Starfield was in full production. Starfield was Bethesda's top priority in the years leading up to its 2023 release; Howard later said that they'd just wanted to answer the fan question (are you making a new Elder Scrolls?) that came up every time they announced something else, like Starfield.

"Just pretend we didn't announce it," he joked. "Doesn't exist. No one's heard a word."How long Sentinel will take to get from here to launch is anybody's guess, although Bloomberg's Jason Schreier said on Bluesky that it's "still more than two years away." When questioned about his prediction, Schreier asserted that it's not a prediction at all, and that he knows "the time frame the game is targeting."

#3733. It looks like Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 had fewer active players at launch in the US compared to last year's Black Ops 7

It's been speculated for a while that Call of Duty may be losing its lustre. Although we don't have concrete data with detailed statistics for each game released in the last several years, there's an observable trend in player numbers that's hard to ignore.

US market analysis firm Circana published some data showing player engagement with Modern Warfare 4 following its launch, and compared them to those by Black Ops 7.

The data is based on Circana's proprietary Player Engagement Tracker, which tracks player activity in the US across Steam and PlayStation, and worldwide on Xbox. According to Circana analyst Mat Piscatella, 19 percent of players on PlayStation played Modern Warfare 4 in the week ending 24th October, compared to 17 percent on Xbox, and 4.2 percent on Steam.

With the exception of Steam, those numbers are down compared to last year's Black Ops 7, which saw 23 percent engagement on PlayStation, 29 percent on Xbox, and a meagre 1.5 percent on Steam during its launch week.

Call of Duty managed to land in the top 10 across all three platforms during the same week ending 24th October, per Circana. In fact, it sat just below Fortnite on PlayStation, which is a decent result.

The large drop in activity on Xbox could be explained by Modern Warfare 4's lack of a day-one release on Game Pass. Black Ops 7 was the second (and last) Call of Duty to launch on Game Pass day-and-date with its premium release. Game Pass availability typically boosts player numbers, though not always sales.

The drop on PlayStation is a little harder to explain, but could be a side effect of the incredibly successful Black Ops 1 & 2 ports released in the summer on PS4 and PS5, which captured lapsed players who may have simply lost interest in modern Call of Duty, regardless of the perceived quality of Modern Warfare 4.

Judging by the data we have access to, such as SteamDB numbers showing Modern Warfare 4's launch compared to Black Ops 7's and other recent releases, there's evidence this year's game perhaps isn't as popular as it could've been.

Indeed, even Activision's tenor when talking about Call of Duty first weekend sales has changed. The publisher issued a single statement following Modern Warfare 4's launch, through Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, which does not even mention the game by name.

"One of the most celebrated Call of Duty games in its 24-year history, and now $40bn in lifetime franchise revenue," Sharma wrote on X. "An incredible milestone. Congrats to the Activision team. And to the players, thank you for being with us."

Last year's Black Ops 7 post-launch statement sidestepped talk of sales and revenue entirely, insteading praising the "great response to the quality and depth of gameplay in Black Ops 7".

I don’t know what’s going on with the Survivor edit. I’m not saying fans can always tell who is going to win halfway through every season, but typically at this point, there are two or three strong contenders who more educated fans have coalesced around. That’s definitely not the case at this point in 51. Everyone is still all over the island with their predictions, and there’s perhaps no better example of that than Kristin Flickinger.

Arguably the most universally liked contestant on 51 with the possible exception of Ori, Kristin has probably gotten the most consistently positive edit of any player. Every single time she’s on the screen, the editors seem invested in making her look good. We got a segment where she showed off her negotiation skills. We got a segment where we saw her winning over her tribemates after the swap. We’ve gotten multiple segments where she showed off her literal survival skills. We’ve gotten confessionals where she’s detailed all the strong relationships she has on the island. We even got a montage of all of her audition tapes over the years.

It’s the kind of edit Survivor players dream about getting, but is it a winner’s edit? Well, fans and so-called Edgic experts are not on the same page at all. Some see her as overwhelmingly the most likely winner, and some see her as very likely to be eliminated deep into the merge but very explicitly prior to the endgame. Let’s talk out both sides.

The case for Kristin as a winner is pretty clear and many in the community are making it, perhaps most prominently RHAP’s Shannon Guss. No one on the show has gotten more consistently positive content, and you could argue that a few times, the show even distorted the truth to make her content even more positive. For example, she was shown dunking on Kilby during the negotiation, even though anecdotal evidence later told us she didn’t necessarily get better supplies. That’s been a recurring theme. Even the negativity she’s gotten, which has mostly been from Maggie confessionals, has framed her more as dangerous than incompetent or annoying.

If you dig a little deeper, however, there is actually some cause for concern with Kristin’s edit. Many in the community think she’s being framed as a fan favorite we’re supposed to be sad about exiting the game deep into the merge, and there’s definitely some evidence for that. First, while she’s been a consistent part of the show, there are actually seven players who have more confessionals than her at this point in the game: Devin, Jelly, Lewis, Kilby, Brady, Ori and Erik. She’s only middle of the pack among the players who are left, and that’s actually really bad considering she was picked for negotiation, went to exile island, got swap screwed and got prominently injured during an episode.

Given all the plot-relevant moments she’s been involved in, it’s actually kind of weird she hasn’t gotten more content, which is probably because it keeps getting cut. An emotional scene between her and the Survivor doctor where she was informed she would be allowed to stay in the game got cut and released as an online exclusive. Another scene from this past episode where she explained what happened on Exile Island to her tribe got cut and also released as an online exclusive. Given she’s only in the middle of the pack on content, if she were the winner, it kind of feels like the show would find reasons to use her, not cut compelling scenes she’s involved in.

To me, the most likely scenario is probably that she gets taken out in the 5 to 7 range. That’s typically the point in the game where all the remaining players work together to eliminate the people they think are most likely to win a jury vote, and as a strong public speaker with great relationships, a compelling backstory and a passion for the game, Kristin screams jury threat. There’s also the pesky issue of fire hanging over her head too. We’ve been repeatedly shown and the other players have repeatedly seen her making fire very quickly. She’s the type of player you have to eliminate before the final four, which is why that range just outside makes so much sense.

I have no idea who is going to win this season (though I can guess who is going to lose) and by extension, I have no idea where Kristin is going to finish. All I know for sure is that she’s delightful, and the editors clearly want us to have positive feelings about her, whether she's the possible host Jeff Probst was referring to or not. Maybe that’s because she’s going to go on and win the whole thing, or maybe that’s because she’s the emotional gut punch we’re going to get when she’s betrayed by other players who are worried she’ll win the jury vote if she gets there.

#3731. Indie game website itch.io expands its AI disclosure filter as 'AI slop' continues to overwhelm Steam and other storefronts

Indie game storefront itch.io has expanded its AI disclosure filters, allowing its users to better separate games made with the controversial technology from those who don't.

This expansion, revealed on its official BlueSky account, includes Itchio's search page which now features a "No AI" box. By ticking this, users can hide any game on the website that features the generative AI disclosure. Games created using generative AI must have this disclosure to be present on the platform, similarly to Steam, although without an option to describe to what extent the tech was used.

This change comes shortly after itch.io also revealed the number of game pages being made on the website each day had doubled in the past two months. And, of course, the number of games downloaded and purchases have not doubled to match this new supply.

itch.io is also facing issues linked to the sheer file size. The storefront has a terms of service policy against AI spam, which it cited shortly after it publicly announced "a couple terabytes of AI slop" had been deleted.

This change comes as the industry as a whole has been clogged with an influx of AI games. Steam Next Fest had a record-breaking number of demo submissions last month. Developers pulled demos in fear of their game being copied, and with Steam saying it's the developer's responsibility to make their games less copyable.

It's an issue that isn't going away any time soon. Even as Claude creator Anthropic has introduced rules preventing unoriginal game clones, alternative AI tools can still be used to create them, and the process of creating games using AI tools will still allow for hastily made, low effort slop. Perhaps filters, like the one itch.io has expanded, is a workable solution to this on-going problem.

#3730. Bachelor Nation's Tanner Courtad Addresses Julianne Hough Dating Rumors

Bachelor Nation’s Tanner Courtad is done dancing around those romance rumors with Dancing With the Stars cohost Julianne Hough.

“That was short-lived, but it was fun,” Tanner, 33, shared on the Tuesday, November 3, episode of iHeartRadio’s “Bachelor Happy Hour” podcast. “I was going to Dancing With the Stars to support Joey [Graziadei], and I was sitting in the front row, and Ezra [Sosa] came over to me, and he goes, ‘Hey, our host thinks you’re cute. Can I give you her number?’”

Spoiler alert: Tanner couldn’t turn down that request.

“I look back at Justin Glaze. I’m like, ‘Did you hear that? Is this a prank?’ I thought Justin was in on it or something,” he continued. “But no, we chatted. I actually met her out in the parking lot. We talked for a couple of minutes, decided to go on a date and talked for a little bit. We went to the park with her dog, got some sushi, hung out for the night and that’s when we got spotted by the paparazzi is picking up sushi.”

In December 2024, cameras did in fact catch Tanner and Julianne, 38, walking around a shopping center in Studio City, Calif. They appeared to stop by The Shops at Sportsmen’s Lodge, which features various shopping, dining and wellness businesses.

“It was very short-lived,” Tanner explained of the pair’s brief tryst. “Julianne’s great, but it was never anything more than just, like, a single singular date.”

Podcast cohosts Charity Lawson and Rachel Recchia dug a little deeper and asked if it was a singular date because of her side.

“Yeah, I think so,” Tanner replied. “I blew it, guys.”

Tanner appeared on Charity’s season of The Bachelorette in 2023 before signing up for Bachelor in Paradise the same year.

While he didn’t find his happily ever after on the ABC reality franchise, the personal trainer was romantically linked to another beloved reality star — Brittany Cartwright.

According to Tanner, however, he was always just friends with The Valley star.

“Brittany’s great. When I first moved out to L.A., I knew nothing about reality TV. I never watched Vanderpump Rules,” he recalled. “I went to the sports bar. It was called Jax’s. I met this owner named Brittany. She’s from Kentucky and she’s bubbly and nice. We started talking, and then I posted a picture with us on Instagram.”

Fans started speculating online in August 2024 that the pair were a hot new couple. Ultimately, Tanner said they were “always just friends.”

“The media just ran away with the story. It was never anything more than a friendship with us,” he said. “But Brittany’s great. And her friends are awesome. It was always just a friendship. There was never anything more there.”

Every Halloween, I think I've seen the year's best celebrity costume, and then somebody comes along and changes my mind. And while there's plenty keeping me entertained on the 2026 TV schedule, former Riverdale stars Madelaine Petsch and Camila Mendes just gave me a fictional show I'd absolutely watch. Petsch and Mendes spent Halloween dressed as Wilma Flintstone and Betty Rubble, respectively, and their ridiculously glamorous photo shoot has me wishing The Real Housewives of Bedrock were an actual series I could binge.

Petsch and Mendes shared the pictures in a joint Instagram post on Halloween, captioning them "The Real Housewives of Bedrock," complete with a bone emoji. Amber Asaly shot the photos, and they look like promotional stills for the most unhinged Bravo spinoff imaginable. Prehistoric sets, dramatic side-eyes, and enough attitude suggest somebody's about to get kicked out of the Bedrock country club. Seriously, take a look:

A post shared by Madelaine Petsch (@madelame)

Since Andy Cohen recently teased the possibility of more Real Housewives cities, I think somebody should put Bedrock on the list. Seriously, who’s Flintmobile’s stone log rollers do I gotta buff to get this thing greenlit?

Petsch nails Wilma's signature look: red curls piled high, a white one-shoulder dress with a jagged hem, and those enormous pearls. Mendes, meanwhile, makes a fantastic Betty in a blue dress, matching hair bow and sleek dark bob. They've kept the recognizable Flintstones details while giving everything a glossy, fashion-editorial makeover. I'd genuinely love to see the rest of their imaginary cast.

The photos are where the joke really takes off. In one, Betty leans over to whisper something into Wilma's ear, while Wilma looks appropriately scandalized. Another pic shows them posing with champagne glasses, and there are shots of the pair lounging among rocky scenery lifted from the cartoon. They even brought two little white dogs into the mix. I'm not sure what the dogs have to do with prehistoric suburbia, I suppose its hard to secure a tiny dino on short notice, so I’m glad the pups got an invite.

As much as I love the outfits, someone in the Instagram comments deserves a gold star for the funniest response to the entire shoot. User @herecomesjoey wrote:

RIP CW, you would’ve greenlit this show by Monday morning 😭👌🏽🔥😍

I've always had a soft spot for how the 1994 live-action Flintstones movie brought Bedrock to life, and these costumes have that same wonderfully ridiculous attention to detail. Only this time, Wilma and Betty look ready for a Bravo reunion special.

They don’t really produce their own original series anymore, but the CW is still on the air, and I laughed harder than I probably should have. Considering these two spent seven seasons on Riverdale, a show that got increasingly bizarre right up through its series finale, a CW-style Flintstones drama feels almost plausible. I can already hear the trailer voice-over: "In Bedrock, everybody has something to hide."

Of course, Petsch and Mendes have a history of taking Halloween costumes very seriously. Just last year, they dressed as Kim Possible and Shego, proving that transforming into beloved cartoon characters is becoming something of an annual tradition for these two. Before that, they joined fellow Riverdale alum Lili Reinhart to dress as the Gotham City Sirens for Halloween, after previously transforming into the Sanderson sisters from Hocus Pocus. This year's costume is a duo rather than a trio, but Reinhart still showed up in the comments with a perfect one-word endorsement: "Icons." I can't argue with her.

What really sells these pictures for me is how completely the actresses commit to the bit. They look ready to feud over a dinner-party seating chart carved into a stone tablet. Unfortunately, The Real Housewives of Bedrock isn't a real series. For now, it's an excellent Halloween photo shoot and another reminder that Petsch and Mendes know how to have fun together long after Riverdale ended. But if anybody wants to commission a pilot, I expect a reunion special hosted by a particularly exhausted Fred Flintstone.

Riverdale is streaming in its entirety with a Netflix subscription.

Ryan graduated from Missouri State University with a BA in English/Creative Writing. An expert in all things horror, Ryan enjoys covering a wide variety of topics. He's also a lifelong comic book fan and an avid watcher of Game of Thrones and House of the Dragon.

#3728. COD: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ patch has nerfed UAV Towers so you're not immediately visible everywhere you go

The Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 patches continue, with the latest delivering some big changes to the game's extraction mode DMZ. The latest hotfix introduced a key balance change to one of DMZ's most controversial mechanics: UAV Towers.

UAV Towers, previously guaranteed to spawn in every Point of Interest (POI) in the map, have now had their spawn logic randomised. Infinity Ward also reduced their spawn rate by 40 percent, meaning you're less likely to find them across the various regions of the map. As noted in the patch notes, that change also prevents multiple towers from spawning the same area. The only exception is the Deadtown area, which factors into DMZ Order progression and requires multiple towers.

By taking away the guarantee that each POI will have at least one UAV Tower, the patch removes one of the core tactics PvP-inclined and aggressive players have been relying on since DMZ's launch. It's common for players to spawn in, and immediately run around activating as many UAV Towers as possible to reveal the movement of enemy players, even if they're not interested in directly engaging them.

Indeed, some of the UAV Towers cover extraction areas, so it's easy for players intending to ruin the day of others as they're extracting to set up elaborate traps. Making matters worse, a particular character trait prevents UAV Towers from expiring, allowing the scans to stay up for the entire match.

Infinity Ward has not commented directly on that trait, but the developer confirmed it's being changed so the Sedative Inhaler - which hides you from UAVs - also works with those trait-upgraded towers, though that change won't arrive until sometime in Season 1.

Finally, today's update further makes it easier to stay undetected by boosting the Sedative Inhaler's duration to 120 seconds, double that of the previous 60, which should help while we wait for larger changes to be implemented.

DMZ has been one of Modern Warfare 4's most discussed modes online. Recently, players discovered what appears to be a separate matchmaking pool for Story Missions that prevents solo sessions from featuring other players, though with some caveats.

Welcome to FOV 90, an FPS column from staff writer Morgan Park. Every other week, I cover topics relevant to first-person shooter enjoyers, spanning everything from multiplayer and singleplayer to the old and the new.

Welcome back to a special election day edition of FOV 90, the only FPS column that insists American readers vote twice today—first on important videogame matters right here, then on crucial *gestures at everything else* matters at your designated polling place.

Today we return from a totally planned hiatus, during which the PC Gamer community settled both the best RTS unit and best horror games, to dispute an issue of far greater significance: The greatest FPS mode of all time. Round 2's matchups reflected an enthusiasm for classic team-based formats with a respectable turnout as well for modern arrivals like Battle Royale. I asked you to make some tough calls and you showed up.

Over 2,500 votes were cast across Round 2 matchups, and the results are in.

A decisive victory in each contest. Every mode I voted for came out on top, which I honestly didn't expect. Sure, TDM over Battle Royale makes sense, but an 82% majority tells me that the most popular shooter format of today has not usurped the classics among PC Gamer readers (same). But even so, this is where I expected Conquest (a chaotic fight over territory) to accept a humble defeat to Bomb Defusal (the gold standard of competitive PvP). I'm glad I was wrong!

Not as much comment sparring went down this time, but I would like to highlight one reader comment that got me thinking:

And here's how PC Gamer's staff reacted to the results:

"What's notable to me about the final four is that they mostly don't put individuals on the spot. In Infection, Battle Royale, and Bomb Defusal, you can wind up being the last survivor, with all the pressure on you to bring it home. That's not really the case in TDM, Conquest, Payload, or CTF, which usually allow unlimited respawns (or in the case of Conquest, end when respawns run out). CTF does require individual flag runner heroism, but as part of a team effort."

"The continued dominance of Payload is vexing to me: I've always thought it was Fine, but an all-conquering hero? Maybe I'm just sore it bodied Gun Game in the first round—I was a fan back when it was a modded Counter-Strike mode first and foremost. If Payload beats out the all time classic, Capture the Flag, this round, we may have to reexamine this whole "democracy" thing."

"CTF had its time, and was at its peak in the various iterations of Tribes, a context in which you could literally swoop in to snatch the banner. But I don't think it stands up if we're evaluating these as modern modes. Otherwise, it's tough to see Bomb Defusal fizzle—Counter-Strike's competitive mode holds up wonderfully as the premier FPS esport, which says a lot given that it's asymmetrical."

But alas, it's time to bury our dead and move on. Round 3 is on!

Read up on the matchups below and vote for your favorite. Round 3 voting closes on Sunday, November 8 at 11:59 PM PDT. The more votes we get, the more interesting the results, so tell your friends! Next week we'll be back to share the results and begin the FINALS.

#3726. The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel is confirmed, finally getting new trailer and full name, 8 years, 4 months, and 23 days after its reveal

Today, Xbox and Bethesda have finally revealed the name and more information about The Elder Scrolls 6. The game, which we now know carries the subtitle Sentinel, was revealed in a special video that took place today, 3rd November 2026, almost exactly 15 years since the launch of The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim and eight years, four months, and 23 days since the first reveal of the title card for The Elder Scrolls 6. That's over 100 months, by the way, or 3067 days, if you want to get specific.

In the trailer, a glimpse of the new game - mostly with some fancy sand physics - before the name, Sentinel, is revealed formally. "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate," says a quote in the video, attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell.

"For 40 years, we've explored new worlds, told unforgettable stories, and gone on incredible adventures together," says a blurb for new video. "From everyone at Bethesda Game Studios, thank you for joining us along this journey, for making these worlds your own, and for inspiring us to keep creating. Here's to 40 more."

This reveal comes after a report last week suggested we'd be seeing more of the highly-anticipated fantasy RPG in November, and which also predicted the name of the game. That report suggested that the title will take place in the Tamriel region of Hammerfell, will touch on the "history of the Elder Scrolls" and will "help uncover the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts". This trailer seems to confirm all that.

Asha Sharma, CEO of Xbox, said she'd played the game in August on a trip to the Bethesda offices, as a giant inflatable rat and a union protest took place outside. Notably, the reveal of the game is taking place not six months after Bethesda suffered sweeping job cuts (alongside many other Microsoft-owned studios) as part of Xbox's "reset".

So why has it taken eight years for Bethesda to show us this game? Previously, Skyrim's lead designer Bruce Nesmith noted that the studio and boss Todd Howard felt pressured to reveal the game to the world because "the pitchforks and torches were out". "[...] Todd's opinion - one which I share, by the way - is that the video game industry has short memories," he said in an interview in 2023. "Those companies that start touting their games years ahead of time, actually, you know, they screw themselves. The best time to start talking about it is six months before release." It's worth noting, then, that this is what Bethesda did with Fallout 4.

Does that hint at a timeline for more Sentinel footage being shown soon, and a potentially sooner-than-we-thought release date? Who knows. If we are going to see the game again anytime soon, it's most likely going to be during The Game Awards 2026, which is taking place on 10th December.

#3725. DWTS’ Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach Break Down Scary Wardrobe Malfunction

Dancing With the Stars pro Daniella Karagach’s costume might have gotten caught on Ezra Frech’s prosthetic leg, but the pair didn’t let it stop them from completing their routine.

“A lot of samba rolls, a lot of practice, hours and hours over and over again. And then, of course, the one time we do it live, my prosthetic gets caught in her fringe,” Frech, 21, exclusively told Us after the Monday, November 2, Disney Night episode. “I literally … my heart dropped to the floor.”

Karagach, 33, jumped in to add, “You still nailed it. You nailed it.”

During the pair’s samba to “Under the Sea” from The Little Mermaid, the fringe on Karagach’s costume briefly got tangled in Frech’s prosthetic before unwrapping itself. While Karagach said she had “no idea” that it had gotten caught at the moment, Frech was internally worried about the situation.

“I was like, ‘Oh my gosh.’ I was like, ‘Oh my gosh.’ I was like, ‘Oh my gosh,’” the Paralympian, who was born without most of his left leg and hand, recalled, while Karagach added of her own reaction, “This is like resistance training. … The fact that it just unwrapped on its own is insane.”

Despite the wardrobe malfunction, Karagach and Frech ultimately received a 37 out of 40 from judges Carrie Ann Inaba, Derek Hough and Bruno Tonioli and guest judge Cynthia Erivo.

“She’s such a massive icon, and she’s so knowledgeable in performance. So to have her here and say those things was out of a dream,” Karagach said of Erivo, 39, while Frech added, “Yeah, I completely agree.”

He continued, “I mean, she will go down as one of the most legendary guest judges, and she brought that energy. Everything she said, you could feel it. Her critiques and her comments are so valuable, period. So when she says something so positive about us, it means so much.”

The pair also received a perfect 40 out of 40 for their group dance number to High School Musical’s “We’re All in This Together.” Frech shared that he had “the best time” working with the group led by team captain Connor Wood.

“Getting to be around such talented dancers, such amazing human beings, we had a blast in the rehearsal studio. Literally so much fun, and we worked really well together,” he said. “And this dance was a fun dance. Our team dance was literally a fun dance. I was having a blast doing it.”

He continued, “They adjusted the choreography for me and put me in positions where I was comfortable. I just appreciate that so much. That consideration, that team chemistry, that’s what helped us go out there and put together a dance that we were all so proud of.”

#3724. The Director Of The Original Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Calls Fixing The Infamous Water Temple ‘Overdue Homework’

Nintendo Switch 2The Legend of ZeldaThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time

Yes, even Eiji Aonuma knows that the original water temple in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, frankly, kind of sucked.

In an Ask the Developer interview today, original Ocarina of Time director and now producer and franchise head Eiji Aonuma was asked about the game’s dungeons, which he was “deeply involved with” in the first game’s development. But when asked about changes to dungeons in general, Aonuma immediately brought up one in particular: the water temple.

The water temple is both an absolutely fantastic dungeon and also one of the most infuriating in the series, at least in its original incarnation. Its main mechanic involves raising and lowering the level of water throughout the dungeon in order to proceed to new areas, with both high and low water being required for certain doorways and paths to be useful. That on its own can be disorienting and confusing, which is part of what makes it so effective. But what was annoying was the need to constantly don and doff the Iron Boots to sink and float in the water. In the original game, Link couldn’t swim, so the only way to get down into the water was to equip the Iron Boots and sink, and then de-equip them to float. But doing this involved opening the game’s menu, navigating to the page they were on, and toggling them from there. Every. Single. Time. Combining this with one required treasure chest in particular hidden under a moving platform that most people struggled to find on their first attempt, and the water temple cemented itself in many people’s childhood memories as a nightmare.

Nintendo has since made the water temple far more reasonable in its 3DS remake, allowing players to set the boots to a single button to put on and remove, and adjusting a cutscene to make the treasure chest’s location more apparent. And from trailers, we’ve known that a similar treatment was going to be applied here. But it’s fascinating to hear Aonuma finally address these memorable problems:

I had some overdue homework: I wanted to do something about the Water Temple I created 28 years ago. (Laughs) Since it became well known for its difficulty in the original game, I had the team make some adjustments in this version. When I designed the Water Temple all those years ago, I wanted to create an experience where simply being underwater was fun. It was a time when there were very few 3D games that even let players go underwater. I enjoy freediving, and what I find fascinating about being underwater is how different everything feels. The sounds change, and it feels like youâre in a completely different space. I wanted to create a place where players could experience those sensations. However, with the dungeonâs complex structure and a lot of item toggling involved, you often had to open the menu screen repeatedly, making it hard to keep track of where you were and which way you were facing. We addressed those issues in this version.

Remake director HokWai Ng added some specifics: item toggling is much easier in the remake, and the team also “changed some of the walls that made it easy to lose your sense of direction to lattice-style structures, making it possible to see the rooms beyond them and get a better sense of the overall space.”

What they don’t discuss in the remake but I’m nonetheless fascinated to see play out is the swimming mechanic. Link couldn’t properly swim underwater in the original game, but in this one, he can. The iron boots serve to ground him on the floor in the dungeon and, I presume, allow him to interact with underwater puzzles in a way he can’t when he’s free swimming. But the new swimming still allows for a level of movement precision that wasn’t possible before, and I’m curious if that changes the puzzles or the dungeon’s approach any.

Only two more days before I find out. Ocarina of Time is out November 5. The rest of the Ask the Developer interview can be found right here.

The new reboot of Baywatch is just a couple of months away. We won’t see it on the 2026 TV schedule, but in the depths of the cold winter in January, we’ll be headed back to the beach on Fox. Two stars of the new version, Stephen Amell and Brooks Nader, recently spoke about some of the stars of the original Baywatch possibly returning in the reboot (other than the couple of former lifeguards who have been announced), and that led Nader to talk about some advice she got from Carmen Electra.

While talking to a gaggle of reporters hyping up the show, Nadar told them (via Deadline):

I spoke to Carmen Electra, and she said…. She just was like, ‘Oh my gosh, this is gonna be great.’ All she said about the series is how much hard work you have to actually put into it and how physically taxing it is on your body. And I heard at the beginning of filming, and I was like, ‘Eh, [I] got this.’ She was totally right in every way possible.

This isn’t the first time that Electra has given this advice to the new cast, telling E! back in June the same thing. It also seems as though the cast has gotten the message, as Amell has talked about all the prep he’s putting in to deal with the long, shirtless days and hours in the Pacific Ocean. Nadar has also joked about how her whole life is now “running in slow motion” since landing the gig.

Though Amell and Nadar were a little coy in their answer about returning stars, only hinting that some big names may show up, they definitely left the door open. Electra, of course, was one of the biggest stars during Baywatch’s original run in the 1990s. Whether she is going to return or not isn’t unknown. She’s said in the past that she is interested in returning (and even donned the old red suit earlier this year), provided she doesn’t have to shoot anything in the water.

Elektra has talked a lot about the new show and how hard it’ll be to recapture the magic of the original show. She knows it’ll be hard to replace icons like Yasmin Bleeth and Pamela Anderson, for example. Nadar isn’t taking the responsibility lightly, though, even perfecting her mouth-to-mouth for the show.

Whether the new show can recapture whatever lightning in a bottle the OG show had remains to be seen, but from all the interviews, it seems the cast knows exactly what the goal is, and they are really going for it.

It's been a good few months for Remedy Entertainment. In its latest financial results, the Finnish game developer announced that its third quarter revenue had more than tripled to €39.6 million ($44.3 million) from the €12.2 million ($13.7 million) it made during the same quarter last year.

That spike in income is all thanks to preorders and launch sales of Control Resonant—of which only the first seven days of sales were counted in Remedy's third quarter figures. On October 15, Resonant sold its millionth copy, making it the fastest-selling game in Remedy history.

"This is our first self-published game of this scale, built on our own Control IP," said Remedy CEO Jean-Charles Gaudechon, who was appointed to the position earlier this year. "Praised by players and critics alike, it marks a defining milestone for the company."

Gaudechon also noted that "close to 50%" of Resonant players were Control newcomers, indicating the sequel had achieved "a key goal" of expanding the audience for Remedy's brand of stylish interdimensional sicko content. Its mission for the immediate future, the CEO said, is to continue delivering Resonant to more interested players—2.4 million of whom still have yet to turn their wishlists into purchases, according to Remedy data.

"Our priority now is to get Control Resonant into the hands of more players. Excellent player reviews, penetration in all our target markets and a substantial outstanding wishlist base give a solid foundation for the game's longer-term sales potential, supported by both organic visibility as well as our targeted marketing activities," Gaudechon said. "As with the launch, we will invest with discipline, prioritizing actions with a clear return."

While Remedy's operating profit margin was still thin for the quarter—1.5% of revenue, or €0.6 million—Resonant's strong launch performance is a welcome change of pace from where the studio was at the end of last year. In November 2025, it had posted an operating loss of €16.4 million thanks to the flop of FBC Firebreak. From the sounds of it, Remedy's aiming to continue that momentum with whatever work it has planned next.

"Alongside the launch of Control Resonant, our other projects are proceeding in the pipeline," Gaudechon said. "Sales over the remainder of the year will ultimately define our financial year 2026. Control Resonant gives us a solid foundation for growth."

#3720. Arc Raiders devs say that using generative AI voice acting was necessary as actors "would just go crazy if they had to read all of that"

CCO states: "We are not in the industry of replacing actors.".

Developers at Embark Studios, the company behind Arc Raiders, have spoken on the use of generative AI voice acting in the extraction shooter. It's argued that the initial use of generative AI line reads was a benefit to the voice actors, as they: "would just go crazy if they had to read all of that".

This comes from a recently released video by Embark, focused on Arc Raider's sound and music. In it, several key members of staff speak on the game's use of generative AI, be it the initial use of it for voice lines, and the gradual replacement of it with human line reads.

Audio director Bence Pajor first spoke about the struggles he ran into at previous studios; how gameplay decisions couldn't be changed because voice lines were already locked in. He describes this as a "true pain", and that it places stress on the writing team, dialogue team, and voice actors who may have scheduling clashes. He said that using reachable voice actors in Stockholm, and using the tools available, made life easier for everyone.

Later in the video, Pajor explained that training data was made with the voice actor's performances. Due to the voice lines being required for each new feature, item, or weapon added into the game, he argues it would be too impractical to record every possible version of a line read. "The actors would just go crazy if they had to read all of that," Pajor said.

Pajor continues by pointing to Arc Raider's many updates and changes since its release in October 2025, it would be impractical to call in voice actors to record lines every time an altered line read needed to happen. Two voice actors present in the video - Jo Rideout (Shani) and Diana Gardner (Celeste) - also shared their feelings on it. Gardner said it was "freeing" that she could take a job somewhere else, without worrying about cancelling other shoots or projects.

However, Gardner would later speak on the topic of her ownership of Celeste's many lines in the game: "The contract seemed so fair [...] so it was a no-brainer in that sense. But I didn't know what to expect once I heard the voice come out. I was like, 'Can I take ownership for the performance?' [...] This is hours of work that I've put in, but can I take ownership for the final product? No."

Even with these proposed benefits to using AI-powered performances, these voice lines are being replaced. Embark CCO Stefan Strandberg said: "we are not in the industry of replacing voice actors", and acknowledges that immersion-breaking experiences many players had when playing Arc Raiders and hearing these performances. Strandberg and Pajor both admit to understanding the AI critique, and point to the work being done to replace what they can.

"We are not in the industry of replacing actors," said Strandberg. "Actually I think quite the opposite. We should celebrate the performance and give them more space. That's something I'm hoping to give to players over the coming years."

Part of this critique over generative AI's use in Arc Raiders came from reviews, including our own. Embark Studios faced similar pushback for gen-AI voice acting in The Finals, however Arc Raider's popularity while using the technology led Nexon to describe it as a "trojan horse" for gen AI's use in small team game development.

#3719. GTA 6 Pre-Load Times, Install Size, And Global Release Times Confirmed

Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VIGTA 6Pre-Load

We’re just over two weeks out from the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 and Rockstar Games has finally revealed all of the details people need to know about getting the digital-only open-world game installed on their gaming console of choice.

The studio also confirmed that, yes, GTA 6 has a whopping 212GB install size, so start making room for that and god help you if you have an Xbox Series S. Here’s everything you need to know about getting GTA 6 ready to play for its release on November 19, 2026.

Digital pre-loading on PlayStation 5 will start globally on Tuesday, November 10 at midnight local time. On Xbox Series X|S, pre-loading begins globally on Tuesday, November 10 at 12 a.m. GMT, which is 7:00 p.m. ET on the previous day, November 9.

If you pre-order GTA 6 digitally, you’ll have access to pre-load the game immediately. If you are waiting for one of the codes in a box to ship to your home or be picked up in store, those will become available starting November 12. You’ll be able to take that code, redeem it, and immediately start pre-loading the game.

That’s a big file size, and console servers are going to get hammered when everyone starts trying to download it at once. To put it in perspective, 212GB is roughly one third of the available storage on a base PS5 and roughly a quarter of the available storage on a 1TB model. On Xbox Series S, it’s closer to half. In addition to taking some time depending on the speed of your internet, you’ll want to make sure you have your library cleared of any non-essential games. Good luck to you if you have children who are constantly swapping between a dozen different games every day.

The global release times for when GTA 6 goes live were previously announced, and unfortunately the U.S. is one of the last time zones to get access to the game.

Yes, the game will have been out in some parts of the world for roughly 18 hours by the time GTA 6 goes live stateside. My advice is to just stay logged out that day.

This pretty patterned pullover makes a soft statement with its muted orange-and-cream diamond pattern, wavy trim and relaxed silhouette. 3. Color Me Cozy: I have plenty of striped sweaters in my closet, but none quite like this one! The chunky ivory knit features colorful, embroidered-looking stripes in navy, burnt orange and burgundy. Plus, the oversized balloon sleeves give it a fun, slouchy silhouette for easy, all-day wear.

4. Plaid Perfection: I love the look of a perfectly layered sweater, but I don’t always have the patience to get two separate pieces to sit just right. This camel-colored knit sweater solves that problem with built-in plaid detailing at the neckline, cuffs and hem, giving me that preppy, put-together look in seconds.

5. Cable-Knit Crush: This is the kind of sweater that makes me want to book a weekend getaway to a cozy mountain cabin. The chunky cable-knit pullover features an intricate mix of braided and diamond-shaped stitching, oversized sleeves and a thick ribbed turtleneck that looks wonderfully cozy.

6. Flower Power: My inner flower child is absolutely obsessed with this daisy-covered knit sweater. The wavy neckline and bottom hem really make me swoon since it adds an extra dose of charm to an already adorable piece.

7. Petal Perfect: I’m not usually one to wish away sweater weather, but this garden-inspired top has me dreaming of spring. The romantic floral pattern and scalloped white neckline adds just enough sweetness to my typically neutral fall wardrobe.

8. Ruffle Romance: Who knew a little gingham could make a navy sweater this adorable? The soft knit pullover features a playful checkered collar, button placket and cuffs, giving it a fun, feminine appearance. Add a pair of tailored trousers, and I’m ready for anything from a morning meeting to an afternoon coffee date.

9. A Little Wild: Sometimes all a plain sweater needs is one really good accessory, and this bow-adorned knit comes with its own! The dramatic leopard-print ribbon adds a fun contrast to the creamy neutral fabric, which I love. It’s exactly what I’d reach for when I want to make a statement without wearing anything particularly bold.

10. Instant Mood Lift: Gray skies don’t mean my wardrobe has to be equally gloomy! The multicolored dot sweater brings sunshine to drab days with a cheerful pattern and surprisingly wearable color palette. I plan to wear it when I want something more exciting than simple basic.

11. Neutral With a Twist: Designed with ruffle-trim details, this striped sweater is one I quickly fell in love with. It has the prettiest chocolate-and-cream color combination, however, the gathered cuffs are what really caught my attention. I love that the sleeves make a statement without getting in the way of an otherwise easy, everyday outfit.

12. Romantic Ruffles: I have a weakness for feminine details, and this ruffled V-neck sweater is making my heart skip a beat. The dramatic cascading ruffles and dainty tie-front neckline give an otherwise simple knit a romantic makeover. Wear it with tailored trousers and delicate gold earrings for a dinner date to look dressed up without sacrificing comfort.

13. Rich Girl-Style: This elegant cream knit has all the makings of something a wealthy Parisian woman would wear to lunch. I adore the wavy black trim and decorative gold buttons, which create the look of a polished cardigan without having to fuss with an actual button-front sweater. The soft, fuzzy texture makes it feel more relaxed for everyday wear, too.

14. Burgundy Blooms: My love for floral sweaters doesn’t end when summer does, especially when they come in rich fall colors! This burgundy flower knit trades traditional pastel blooms for oversized wine-colored daisies. It’s a fun way to embrace the season’s burgundy trend without committing to another solid-colored sweater.

15. Sweet But Sophisticated: Ruffles can sometimes feel a little too precious for everyday wear, but this diamond-textured sweater gets them just right. The frills at the neckline and cuffs add a subtle romantic touch. And if beige isn’t your thing, there are five other shades to choose from, including olive green and baby blue.

16. Compliment Magnet: I have a feeling this statement floral pullover will get more compliments than half the sweaters in my closet. The oversized blue blooms are impossible to miss, and the soft ivory background keeps the whole look wearable. It also comes in six other color combinations, so there’s something for just about every fall wardrobe.

17. Luxe Lace: There’s something about chocolate brown and delicate lace that feels so romantic. This feminine crewneck sweater combines the two beautifully, with an intricate scalloped hem that makes even simple white trousers look special. I’d happily wear it to a cozy dinner date with gold jewelry and my favorite boots.

How much are the shocking claims hurting the Duchess?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Thomas Markle, father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, is in the news again for all the wrong reasons. He’s made a habit of this over the years, but the latest bombshell pedophilia claims are beyond anything he’s done in the past. It’s a sordid story to say the least, and (at least according to one report) it’s so bad that it’s affecting Meghan Markle’s business negatively. Meghan has been estranged from Thomas for years, but the allegations are so controversial that they could be coming into play here, according to Rob Shuter on his Substack, Naughty But Nice.

According to an unnamed source of Shuter’s, Meghan’s lifestyle brand, including her Emmy-nominated lifestyle show that you can check out with a Netflix subscription, is in “full-blown crisis” amid the allegations. Thomas’ son (Meghan’s half-brother) reported that he found child pornography in Thomas’ home in the Philippines and alerted authorities there and in the United States. The source told Shuter:

Sales were already terrible when the allegations first surfaced. Now they’ve fallen to zero, This is about something far more serious than a business setback. These are deeply disturbing allegations, and people are horrified. Nobody wants to be sold a fantasy of family happiness while questions this serious remain unanswered.

Though the Duchess has distanced herself from her father over the years, including leaving him off the invitation list for her wedding to Prince Harry in 2018, according to Shuter’s supposed source, that doesn’t matter. The source added:

Meghan cannot simply turn the page and pretend this isn’t happening. The allegations are extremely serious, and people want answers. Her lifestyle brand is now caught in the middle of a family scandal that refuses to go away.

Obviously, these are very serious allegations.

In late October, The Sun reported that Thomas was being investigated for a cache of “hundreds, if not thousands” of images and videos in boxes in this home, discovered by his son, Thomas Jr., Meghan’s half-brother. The younger Thomas reported what he found to the FBI in the U.S., where Thomas Sr. is currently living after surgery to amputate one of his legs.

That report was followed up by another from The Sun last week that Meghan knew of the images and reportedly sent Thomas Sr. last December, as he recovered from the surgery. In the letter, Meghan allegedly told Thomas Sr. that she had been aware of the allegations as early as 2019. Meghan has not been in contact with Thomas Sr. in years, and reportedly has banned her father from ever meeting her two children with Prince Harry.

Thomas Jr. has also been estranged from the Duchess for years, after siding with their father many years ago, something he now regrets, telling The Sun:

I now know I have been protecting the wrong person for the past nine years. Having seen what I have seen, I believe the man I’ve been defending and caring for is a monster.

Whether all of this is really affecting Meghan Markle’s business, as Shuter claims, is impossible to know for sure. As I said, it’s not like Meghan is close to her father, and fans of the Duchess have long known their history (though SNL UK is still taking their shots, of course), but these are serious allegations, so it’s not unreasonable to think it's possibly been bad for the business.
